name: fx30_v5.00
summary: Locked skeleton - NOT verified on hardware. No memory offsets yet: the FX30 shares the A6700's BIONZ XR chip and 26 MP APS-C sensor, so its equivalent sites are expected to be close by, but unconfirmed until dumped. Every write below is a placeholder pending --dump-ram (read candidate offsets off a real body) and --scan-dump (locate them from a target firmware dump against the verified A6700 profile's signatures). Do not run --confirm-ram-write against this file - it has zero resolved writes and the injector refuses that on purpose.
verify_rule: Read every write's address first; each must equal its 'stock'. If any site differs, abort before writing one byte (wrong firmware or already patched). Not yet applicable here - there are no writes yet.

steps.label: raw write buffer (memory manager)
steps.desc: PENDING. On the verified A6700 this enlarges the raw write-buffer size words for a taller frame. Locate the equivalent site on this body via --scan-dump against the A6700 profile's L13 stock signature, then confirm the exact offset(s) with --dump-ram before adding any write here.

steps.label: encoder output size
steps.desc: PENDING. On the verified A6700 this sets the movie-writer output size word. Same approach as L13: --scan-dump to locate, --dump-ram to confirm, before adding any write here.

steps.label: screen / display fit
steps.desc: PENDING. On the verified A6700 this clears the letterbox fit and panel vertical-offset words. Same approach as L13: --scan-dump to locate, --dump-ram to confirm, before adding any write here.

notes: L19 is deliberately excluded from this skeleton. On the verified A6700, the L19 (high-speed-only) encoder rebooted the kernel on the STILL->MOVIE switch (see ../RESEARCH.md) - M19 was the stable replacement there. Until an equivalent encoder path is dumped and read-only-verified on this body, do not add an L19-style step here.
This file ships with zero resolved writes on purpose - host-injector/src/inject.rs refuses --confirm-ram-write on any profile with no resolved writes, pointing back to --dump-ram / --scan-dump.
See the root README's "Contributing a New BIONZ XR Body" section for the full --dump-ram -> --scan-dump -> --verify-only workflow this skeleton is meant to be filled in by.
